newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends higher on StatsCan data, CBOT soy.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends higher on StatsCan data, CBOT soy.

text.p: WCE canola futures closed higher, boosted by sharp gains in old crop CBOT soybeans and bullish planting intentions data issued by Statistics Canada, floor sources said.
"We were up initially on the StatsCan report and Chicago (soybeans) kept us up," one WCE oilseed trader said.
There were also reports that Japan bought 5,000 to 6,000 tonnes of Canadian canola overnight and export-related futures buying was noted. July canola closed up $6.20 at $433.50.
StatsCan put Canadian canola planting intentions at 11.6 million acres, up 30 percent from last year but below most trade expectations which ranged from around 12.0 million to 12.75 million.
The July WCE futures crush profit margin rose to -7.27 Wednesday from -8.50 Tuesday.

Flaxseed closed lower although old crop values were underpinned by talk that May longs may need to take delivery to satisfy export demand. The first delivery day for the May contract is Thursday. May ended off $1.00 at $340.50.
Bearish StatsCan plantings data weighed on new crop. Flaxseed acreage was seen up 53 percent at 2.3 million.
Feedgrains ended slightly higher, boosted by spillover strength from CBOT grains.
July western barley closed up $1.10 at $140.90 with July wheat up $0.60 at $170.20.
New crop feed peas were weak following a bearish StatsCan report. Oct ended off US$2.00 at US$194.00.
October oats ended up US$1.50 at US$121.00.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
